question: Can Arbiter choose companion CXL placement online without a per-benchmark profile?

sources.title: Bandwidth-Aware Page Placement in NUMA Systems
sources.finding: Online hill climbing uses resource stalls; authors also require initialization at a stable phase and discuss amortization and local optima. This supports online ratio search, not the sufficiency of stall metrics for contended retries.

sources.title: Tiered Memory Management: Access Latency is the Key! (Colloid)
sources.finding: Uses measured per-tier queue occupancy/request rates to balance access latencies and limits migration each quantum. Useful for bandwidth/latency adaptation; not a proof that minimizing memory latency optimizes Arbiter's contention workloads.

sources.title: Application Heartbeats
sources.finding: Application progress differs from instruction execution, which can include spinning. Explicit progress is semantically stronger than IPC, but manual application annotations conflict with the no-benchmark-edit constraint.

sources.title: Linux page migration
sources.finding: Physical pages can migrate without changing virtual addresses; accesses can block while migration entries are present.

sources.title: move_pages(2)
sources.finding: Per-page status and partial failure must be checked. Moving a page does not update its NUMA allocation policy.

sources.title: LLVM 18.1.8 loop terminology
sources.finding: Latches/backedges and exits define structural loop progress, not semantic application requests.

inference: Compiler-discovered common-loop completions are a portable candidate progress proxy. A fixed-trip loop can publish a batched count at its dedicated exit, excluding inner retry spins. This must be validated per program structure; it is not a universal automatic throughput oracle.
prototype_scope: One unambiguous common loop domain. No argv/symbol-name/per-input lookup in controller. All deployments use the same timing, search ladder, hysteresis and 4 GiB resident companion budget. Existing seeds stay fixed. Multiple/ambiguous domains retain seed-only rewrite. This prototype does not re-explore from zero after a later improvement phase.
